label: Page has broken image
why: Broken images leave empty boxes and hurt user trust.
how: Fix the image URL or re-upload the missing file in WordPress Media Library.

label: Page has broken CSS
why: Missing stylesheets break page layout and mobile usability.
how: Restore the missing CSS file or clear and rebuild your caching plugin's minified CSS.

label: Page has broken JavaScript
why: Broken scripts can stop menus, forms, and interactive features from working.
how: Fix the script path or disable the conflicting plugin asset in your optimization settings.

label: Image redirects
why: Redirected images add extra network round trips and slow down page rendering.
how: Update image URLs to point directly to their final destination file.

label: CSS redirects
why: Redirected stylesheets delay render-blocking CSS downloads.
how: Update the stylesheet link in your theme or plugin to use the final target URL.

label: JavaScript redirects
why: Redirected scripts add extra network latency before execution.
how: Update the script source URL to point directly to the final destination file.

label: Image file size too large
why: Oversized images consume mobile data and slow down Largest Contentful Paint.
how: Compress images and serve modern formats like WebP using a plugin such as ShortPixel or Imagify.

label: CSS file size too large
why: Large CSS files take longer to download and parse before the page renders.
how: Minify CSS and remove unused styles using your caching plugin or theme asset manager.

label: JavaScript file size too large
why: Heavy JavaScript files delay page interactivity and hurt Core Web Vitals.
how: Minify scripts, defer non-critical JS, and remove unused plugins that load heavy bundles.

label: HTTPS page links to HTTP image
why: Loading insecure images on HTTPS pages triggers browser mixed-content warnings.
how: Update image URLs to HTTPS or run a search-and-replace in WordPress to fix HTTP asset links.

label: HTTPS page links to HTTP CSS
why: Modern browsers block insecure HTTP stylesheets on HTTPS pages, breaking layout.
how: Change the stylesheet URL to HTTPS in your theme settings or enforce HTTPS sitewide.

label: HTTPS page links to HTTP JavaScript
why: Browsers block insecure HTTP scripts on HTTPS pages, breaking page functionality.
how: Update the script URL to HTTPS in your theme, plugin, or custom code snippets.

label: Canonical from HTTP to HTTPS
why: HTTP pages canonicalizing to HTTPS should redirect directly instead of relying on tags.
how: Set up a server-level 301 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS in Cloudflare or your web server.

label: Canonical from HTTPS to HTTP
why: Pointing a secure page's canonical to HTTP confuses Google and risks indexing insecure URLs.
how: Update the canonical tag to use the HTTPS version of the URL.

label: Canonical points to 4XX
why: Pointing a canonical tag to a dead error page tells Google not to index valid content.
how: Change the canonical URL to a live 200 OK page in your SEO plugin settings.

label: Canonical points to 5XX
why: Pointing a canonical tag to a broken server-error URL prevents proper indexing.
how: Fix the server error on the target URL or update the canonical to a working 200 page.

label: Canonical points to redirect
why: Canonical tags should point directly to the final destination URL, not a redirect.
how: Update the canonical tag in Yoast or Rank Math to the final 200 OK URL.

label: Non-canonical page specified as canonical one
why: Chaining canonical tags across multiple pages sends mixed signals to search engines.
how: Point the canonical tag directly to the single primary version of the page.

label: Canonical URL has no incoming internal links
why: If the chosen canonical page has zero internal links, Google may ignore the canonical.
how: Add internal links pointing directly to the canonical URL from relevant pages.

label: Noindex follow page
why: Google excludes this page from search results while still following its links.
how: Keep as-is for thin utility pages, or remove noindex in your SEO plugin if it should rank.

label: Noindex and nofollow page
why: Google excludes this page from search and will not pass link equity through it.
how: Remove noindex/nofollow if this page should rank or help Google discover linked pages.

label: Nofollow page
why: A page-level nofollow directive stops Google from following any links on this page.
how: Remove the nofollow robots directive unless you intentionally want to block all outbound links.

label: Noindex in HTML and HTTP header
why: Duplicate noindex rules in both HTML meta tags and HTTP headers are redundant.
how: Keep the noindex rule in one place—usually the meta robots tag—and remove the duplicate.

label: Nofollow in HTML and HTTP header
why: Duplicate nofollow rules in both HTML meta tags and HTTP headers are redundant.
how: Remove the redundant directive so nofollow is defined cleanly in a single place.

label: Redirect chain too long
why: Long redirect chains waste crawl budget, slow down users, and dilute link signals.
how: Update redirects so the initial URL 301-redirects in a single hop to the final URL.

label: Broken redirect
why: A redirect leading to a 4XX or 5XX error traps visitors and crawlers in a dead end.
how: Update the redirect target in your redirection plugin or server config to a live 200 page.

label: HTTPS to HTTP redirect
why: Redirecting secure HTTPS traffic back to unencrypted HTTP exposes users and hurts rankings.
how: Fix your server or Cloudflare SSL rules so all redirects point to HTTPS.

label: Meta refresh redirect
why: HTML meta refresh redirects are slower and pass weaker SEO signals than 301 redirects.
how: Replace the meta refresh tag with a proper server-side 301 HTTP redirect.

label: 3XX redirect in sitemap
why: XML sitemaps should only list final 200 OK indexable URLs, not redirecting URLs.
how: Regenerate your XML sitemap in your SEO plugin so redirected URLs are excluded.

label: 4XX page in sitemap
why: Listing dead 404/410 pages in your sitemap wastes crawl budget and sends bad signals.
how: Remove deleted URLs from your sitemap or restore the missing pages.

label: 5XX page in sitemap
why: Listing server-error URLs in your sitemap causes search engines to distrust sitemap quality.
how: Fix the server error on those URLs or remove them from the XML sitemap.

label: Non-canonical page in sitemap
why: Including non-canonical URLs in your sitemap contradicts your canonical tags.
how: Exclude non-canonical URLs from your SEO plugin's XML sitemap settings.

label: Indexable page not in sitemap
why: Valuable indexable pages missing from your sitemap may be discovered or recrawled slower.
how: Include this post type or taxonomy in your SEO plugin's XML sitemap configuration.

label: Page in multiple sitemaps
why: Listing the same URL across multiple sitemaps creates redundant crawl work.
how: Check your SEO plugin settings to ensure only one sitemap generator is active.

label: Page from sitemap timed out
why: Crawlers timed out trying to fetch a URL listed in your XML sitemap.
how: Check server performance and response times for the slow URL, or remove it from the sitemap.

label: Page has nofollow incoming internal links only
why: If every internal link to a page is nofollow, Google may treat it as low priority.
how: Remove the rel="nofollow" attribute from internal links pointing to this page.

label: Page has nofollow and dofollow incoming internal links
why: Mixing nofollow and dofollow internal links to the same page sends inconsistent signals.
how: Make internal links to this page consistently dofollow unless a specific widget requires nofollow.

label: Page has no outgoing links
why: Dead-end pages with zero outgoing links trap visitors and stop link equity from flowing.
how: Add helpful contextual internal links to related articles or key category pages.

label: Page has nofollow outgoing internal links
why: Using nofollow on internal links blocks link equity flow and wastes crawl discovery.
how: Remove rel="nofollow" from internal links in your content, menus, or widgets.

label: Redirected page has no incoming internal links
why: Legacy redirect URLs with zero internal links are safe to keep if external backlinks exist.
how: Verify if external backlinks point to it; if not, clean up unused redirect rules.

label: HTTPS page has internal links to HTTP
why: Internal HTTP links on an HTTPS site cause extra redirects and mixed-content risks.
how: Update internal links to HTTPS using a database search-and-replace plugin in WordPress.

label: External link broken (4XX)
why: Outbound links to dead 404 pages frustrate readers and lower content quality.
how: Replace the broken external link with a working source or remove the link.

label: External link server error (5XX)
why: An external site you link to is currently returning a server error.
how: Recheck the external URL later and replace it if the target site remains down.

label: External link redirects (3XX)
why: Outbound links that redirect take longer for visitors to load.
how: Update the outbound link URL to point directly to its final destination.

label: Multiple title tags
why: Multiple title tags on one page confuse search engines about which title to display.
how: Check your theme header.php and SEO plugin to remove the duplicate title tag.

label: Multiple meta description tags
why: Multiple meta descriptions make search snippet selection unpredictable.
how: Disable duplicate meta tag output in your theme so only your SEO plugin outputs it.

label: Hreflang annotation invalid
why: Invalid language or region codes cause Google to ignore your hreflang tags completely.
how: Fix the hreflang code to use valid ISO 639-1 language and ISO 3166-1 region formats.

label: Missing reciprocal hreflang
why: Google ignores hreflang annotations unless every linked language page links back.
how: Add the missing return hreflang tag on the alternate language page.

label: Hreflang to broken page
why: Hreflang tags pointing to 4XX or 5XX error pages break international targeting.
how: Update the hreflang tag to point to a live 200 OK translated page.

label: Hreflang to redirect
why: Hreflang annotations should point directly to final URLs, not redirects.
how: Update the hreflang URL in your multilingual plugin to the final 200 destination.

label: Hreflang to non-canonical page
why: Pointing hreflang to a non-canonical URL creates conflicting indexing signals.
how: Ensure all hreflang URLs point strictly to self-referencing canonical pages.

label: Self-referencing hreflang missing
why: Each language version must include a hreflang tag pointing to itself.
how: Configure your multilingual plugin to output a self-referencing hreflang tag on every page.

label: X-default hreflang missing
why: An x-default tag tells Google which fallback page to show unmatched international users.
how: Add an hreflang="x-default" tag pointing to your primary or language-selector page.

label: Hreflang and HTML lang mismatch
why: Conflicting hreflang and HTML lang attributes send mixed language signals to crawlers.
how: Align the HTML lang attribute with the page's primary hreflang language code.

label: More than one page for same language in hreflang
why: Assigning two different URLs to the same language-region code confuses search engines.
how: Ensure each language or locale code maps to only one unique URL per page set.

label: Page referenced for more than one language in hreflang
why: Pointing multiple language codes to the exact same URL usually indicates misconfiguration.
how: Assign distinct translated URLs per language or use a single broad language code.

label: HTML lang attribute invalid
why: An invalid HTML lang code hurts screen readers and browser translation tools.
how: Set a valid ISO language code in WordPress Settings > General or your theme header.

label: Open Graph URL not matching canonical
why: Mismatched og:url and canonical tags can split social share counts and confuse crawlers.
how: Set og:url to match the exact canonical URL in your SEO plugin's social settings.

label: Open Graph tags incomplete
why: Missing og:title, og:description, or og:image causes poor previews when shared on social media.
how: Fill in the social title, description, and featured image in Yoast or Rank Math.

label: Structured data JSON parsing error
why: Syntax errors in JSON-LD prevent Google from reading your schema and showing rich results.
how: Validate the JSON-LD snippet in Google's Rich Results Test and fix broken quotes or commas.

label: Structured data missing required property
why: Schema missing required fields is ineligible for Google rich snippets.
how: Add the missing required fields in your schema plugin or structured data block.

label: Structured data invalid date format
why: Dates in schema must follow ISO 8601 format or Google may ignore them.
how: Format datePublished and dateModified as YYYY-MM-DD or full ISO 8601 timestamps.

label: Structured data image missing
why: Many rich result types require a valid image URL to display visual enhancements.
how: Assign a featured image in WordPress so your SEO plugin includes it in schema markup.

label: JavaScript render-blocking
why: Scripts loaded in the head without defer or async delay first paint for visitors.
how: Defer non-critical JavaScript using a performance plugin like WP Rocket or LiteSpeed Cache.

label: CSS render-blocking
why: External stylesheets block rendering until downloaded and parsed by the browser.
how: Inline critical CSS and defer non-critical stylesheets in your caching plugin.

label: Largest Contentful Paint image lazy-loaded
why: Lazy-loading the main above-the-fold hero image delays Largest Contentful Paint.
how: Exclude your hero or featured image from lazy loading and add fetchpriority="high".

label: Title changed since last audit
why: The page title changed since the previous crawl, which can impact click-through rates.
how: Confirm the title update was intentional and monitor rankings and clicks in Search Console.

label: H1 changed since last audit
why: The main H1 heading changed since the last crawl, which may affect keyword relevance.
how: Review the new H1 heading to ensure it accurately reflects the page's target topic.

label: Meta description changed since last audit
why: The meta description changed since the previous crawl, which may alter search snippets.
how: Verify the new description reads well and encourages clicks from search results.

label: Word count changed a lot since last audit
why: A major drop or spike in word count may indicate accidental content loss or template issues.
how: Inspect the live page to make sure main content blocks were not accidentally removed.

label: Indexable page became non-indexable
why: A previously indexable page is now blocked from Google, risking sudden traffic loss.
how: Check robots meta tags, canonicals, and HTTP status to restore indexability if unintended.

label: 3XX page receives Google clicks
why: Google is still sending organic clicks to a redirecting URL instead of the final page.
how: Ensure canonicals, internal links, and sitemaps point to the final 200 URL so Google updates its index.

label: 4XX page receives Google clicks
why: Searchers are clicking through from Google straight onto a broken 404 error page.
how: Restore the content or 301-redirect the broken URL to the closest relevant page immediately.

label: 5XX page receives Google clicks
why: Google is sending visitors to a URL failing with a server error.
how: Investigate server error logs and restore the page right away to stop losing organic traffic.

label: Noindex page receives Google clicks
why: A page marked noindex is still receiving organic search clicks and may soon drop out.
how: Remove the noindex tag immediately if you want to keep this organic search traffic.

label: Non-canonical page receives Google clicks
why: Google is ranking and sending clicks to an alternate URL rather than your chosen canonical.
how: Review whether the ranking URL should be the true canonical or consolidate signals with a 301 redirect.

label: Google clicks dropped
why: Organic search clicks to this page dropped sharply compared to the previous period.
how: Check Search Console queries for ranking drops, update stale content, and check competitors.

label: Page dropped out of Google top 10
why: This page fell from page one of Google results, which usually cuts clicks sharply.
how: Refresh the page content, strengthen internal links, and check search intent against top results.
